$comment: Realisation for Biblical Hebrew (docs/rules/hbo.md; docs/rules-design.md). realise/hbo-engine runs on zz, an invented fixture language given whole, for what the engine gained with hbo's rules: a lexeme's form that holds only before something in its token (`before`: a stem before a suffixed pronoun), a rewrite that holds only of a token in a context (`when: {context}`: bound by a maqaf, pause), and the free variants of a cell (`variant`, `variants`: ADR 0145, both accepted, the first shown). realise/hbo runs hbo's own rules and lexicon (lexicons/hbo/language.yaml, lexemes.yaml) with `spellings: false`, as the compiler's check of the tokens does: one vector or more per branch of every rule, each a form the course writes (its item in the note).

vectors.note: A form with `before` holds where the rest of the token begins as it says: the stem before the suffix.
Where the rest of the token does not hold it, the lexeme's own form.
A lexeme realised alone (a paradigm's cell) has nothing after it: a form with `before` never holds.
In a cell a rule gives (the plural), the form with `before` takes the rule's place before the suffix.
And alone, the rule's.
An allomorph's `after` may name the feature values of its token's base's cell: the plural's series.
Where the cell has not those values, the next allomorph, here the one with no condition.
Its part of speech: the token's base, for a lexeme that follows it.
Its class.
A free allomorph is never chosen of itself; the token with it in place is an alternative.
One with conditions, where they hold.
A form that names no feature values is a token's that chooses none.
It is no cell's: a token that chooses values has the rules' (here the citation form).
A rewrite whose `when` names a context holds of a token in it.
And of no other.
A token in another context.
A token in two contexts; the rest of `when` must hold too.
Two free variants of a cell: the first, and how many there are.
`variant` realises another.
As a token.
A variant the cell does not have.
Nor where there is one form.
